Human body is our strongest distributing category. The top reach came from counterintuitive direct claims about your own body, such as 'You're shorter tonight than this morning' (108 reach, 65.1 skip) and 'recorded voice' (98, 66.7 skip). The nasal cycle has not been covered and fits that pattern: it is a direct-claim hook the viewer can test on the spot. That invites comments and rewatches. hook: You breathe mostly through one nostril

slides.title: The nasal cycle
slides.body: Tissue inside one nostril swells while the other opens up.

slides.title: They swap shifts
slides.body: Every few hours, your nervous system switches which nostril works harder.
slides.image_prompt: An hourglass beside two glass tubes, air bubbles flowing strongly through one tube and faintly through the other, calm blue studio lighting

slides.title: Try it now
slides.body: Breathe out onto a cold mirror: one fog patch is usually bigger.

cta: Follow for a new body fact daily
caption:
Right now, one of your nostrils is doing most of the breathing. Tissue inside your nose swells on one side and shrinks on the other, and the roles swap every few hours. It's called the nasal cycle, and most people never notice it.

Your autonomic nervous system runs it automatically, the same system that controls your heartbeat. Lying on your side also tends to congest the lower nostril. Follow for one body fact your brain won't believe, every day.

Cover one nostril, then the other: which one is winning right now?
